question: A shopkeeper bought an item for ₹500 and sold it for ₹650. What is the profit percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Selling Price (SP)** = 500 : 650 = 10 : 13.

Profit units = 13 − 10 = 3 units.

**Profit Percentage** = (Profit Units / CP Units) × 100 = (3 / 10) × 100 = 30%.

**∴ The correct answer is 30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price (CP)** of the item = ₹500

**Selling Price (SP)** of the item = ₹650

**Formula Used:**

Profit = **Selling Price** − **Cost Price**

**Profit Percentage** = (Profit / **Cost Price**) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/709df304721fed5850931a6272f4021bb607d0dfb88a0a61083ff62ff0152092.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit = ₹650 − ₹500

⇒ Profit = ₹150

⇒ Profit % = (150 / 500) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 150 / 5

⇒ Profit % = 30%

**∴ The correct answer is 30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When SP is less than CP, Loss % = [(CP − SP) / CP] × 100.

Selling Price Formula

To find SP when CP and Profit % are known: SP = [CP × (100 + Profit %)] / 100.

Cost Price Formula

To find CP when SP and Profit % are known: CP = [SP × 100] / (100 + Profit %).
